evidence_items.explanation: The contemporary synthesis documents broad capability gaps, including failures on simple reasoning and inability to independently execute long projects. This supports the inference that broadly human-level general intelligence had not been demonstrated, while the report leaves future scaling disputed.

The developer describes the pretraining method and separately describes post-training alignment. This anchors the distinction between scaled pretraining and capabilities of a complete deployed system; it does not independently settle AGI.

evidence_items.explanation: The evaluator recognizes a substantial breakthrough but does not regard o3 as AGI. Because this was a system using additional computation at use time, its results are context rather than a direct test of pure pretraining.

This is material competing evidence: the authors describe broad capabilities and characterize GPT-4 as an early, incomplete AGI. Their qualified interpretation does not establish the broad human-level standard used here, but shows why 'clearly' is stronger than the consensus warrants.

unresolved_gaps: There is no universally accepted AGI test.
Public disclosures do not fully isolate the contribution of pretraining from every other training stage.
The cited scientific synthesis predates the post by several weeks and cannot certify every private or newly announced system.
